reconstructed_captions.21: A hand applies adhesive to the edge of a cut piece of black leather.
reconstructed_captions.22: Two pieces of leather are carefully aligned and pressed together to bond.
reconstructed_captions.23: A hand uses a wing divider tool to scribe a stitching guideline along the leather's edge.
reconstructed_captions.24: A stitching chisel is positioned on the guideline, ready to punch holes.
reconstructed_captions.25: A mallet strikes the chisel, creating a row of evenly spaced stitching holes.
reconstructed_captions.26: The process is repeated along the entire edge to prepare for stitching.
reconstructed_captions.27: A close-up shows two needles with thread being prepared for a saddle stitch.
reconstructed_captions.28: A hand begins saddle stitching, passing a needle through the first hole.
reconstructed_captions.29: The second needle is passed through the same hole from the opposite side.
reconstructed_captions.30: The thread is pulled tight, creating a strong, durable lock stitch.
reconstructed_captions.31: The stitching continues meticulously along the punched holes.
reconstructed_captions.32: A close-up view highlights the neat and uniform hand-stitching.
reconstructed_captions.33: The final stitches are made to complete the seam.
reconstructed_captions.34: The thread is tied off and trimmed close to the leather.
reconstructed_captions.35: A lighter is used to carefully melt the thread ends to secure the stitch.
